info.name: VideoGame Platform Backend - Catalogue Administration
info.description: Executable #247, #248, #342, #458 and #450 examples for an authenticated local OIDC session holding the catalogue-operator client role. Sign in through Keycloak in a browser and sync the localhost cookie into Postman; the first request stores the session-bound CSRF token, and no OAuth token or credential belongs in this collection. The last request asks for a one-day synchronization: without provider credentials it is rejected as SYNCHRONIZATION_DISABLED, otherwise it is accepted or answered as already running. The stop and abandonment requests name a run that history never holds, so they never stop or abandon a real run: they prove CSRF enforcement and the stable not-found answer. Anonymous rejection is covered by the session collection and non-operator rejection by the backend integration tests and the real identity gate. Historical #246 reads and command safety examples are included. Normal collection execution never starts a historical import. The explicit-start example is guarded by enableHistoricalStart=true and a deliberately small interval, and stores only the opaque target identity. Stop/resume refusal examples use an unknown identity. Translation examples read coverage and execution and exercise stale-command refusal without changing any execution. Editorial attention examples (#458) read the prompt and lists, preview a sample file and exercise the refusals; the collection never loads or deletes a real list. Product settings examples (#450) read the settings, store their revision and exercise the CSRF, stale-revision, unknown-key, out-of-range and cross-setting refusals; the collection never changes a real setting.
